about: The scripted AI lesson for g5-nigeria (2026-11-19, Phase B, brief docs/briefs/2026-11-15-script-four-topics.md): every word she sees is written here once and checked (tools/check-script.js, tools/review-lesson.js --script). The AI only marks her typed answers (choosing a branch written here), answers her own questions, and sorts her messages. It opens with two recall questions from g5-development.

steps.text: Welcome! This lesson is a case study of one country, Nigeria: where it is, why it matters, how its economy is changing, and what that means for its people and its environment.

steps.question: First, two quick questions from the last lesson, on development. What do we call a country whose economy has started to grow fast as it builds up industry?
steps.right: Yes: an NEE, a newly emerging economy.

wrong.other: Not quite: a newly emerging economy, an NEE.
wrong.lic: Not quite: an LIC is one of the poorest countries. Fast growth through industry makes an NEE.
wrong.hic: Not quite: an HIC is already rich. Fast growth through industry makes an NEE.

idk.hint: Look for the one with "emerging" in it: that word means starting to grow.

steps.answerWhy: A country growing fast as it builds up industry is a newly emerging economy, an NEE.

steps.question: Second: GNI per head measures…?
steps.right: Yes: a country's yearly income shared out equally between its people.

wrong.other: Not quite: the mean income per person.
wrong.life: Not quite: that is life expectancy. GNI per head is the mean income per person.
wrong.imr: Not quite: that is infant mortality. GNI per head is the mean income per person.

idk.hint: GNI stands for gross national income. Which option is about income?

steps.answerWhy: GNI per head is a country's yearly income shared out equally between its people.

steps.text: Now this lesson. Nigeria is in West Africa, on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea, the part of the Atlantic Ocean south of West Africa. With about 238 million people, it has more people than any other African country.
Nigeria is an NEE. Its economy is worth about $291 billion a year, but its GNI per head is only $1,360 a year, compared with $54,550 in the UK. So many Nigerians are still poor.
How much a country matters within its own part of the world is its regional importance. Within West Africa, Nigeria has the biggest economy.
Nigeria is the biggest member of ECOWAS, a group of West African countries working to make trade between them easier.
Globally, across the whole world, Nigeria matters as a big oil exporter, selling oil to other countries, and its films and music are watched and heard far beyond Africa.

steps.question: An exam asks: "Outline one way in which Nigeria is regionally important." Which answer fits?

options.text: It has the biggest economy in West Africa
Its oil is sold all over the world

steps.right: Yes: regional means within its part of the world, West Africa.

wrong.other: Not quite: it has the biggest economy in West Africa.
wrong.global: Selling oil worldwide is global importance. Regional means within West Africa: it has the biggest economy there.
wrong.coast: Not quite: a coastline is a fact about its location, not its importance. Regionally, it has the biggest economy in West Africa.

idk.hint: Regional means within its own part of the world. Nigeria's part of the world is West Africa.

steps.answerWhy: Regionally, within West Africa, Nigeria has the biggest economy.

steps.text: The wider context of the country matters too. Britain ruled Nigeria until independence. Since then Nigeria has had military governments as well as elected ones.
Nigeria has hundreds of ethnic groups: peoples with their own languages and customs. The largest are the Hausa-Fulani in the north and the Yoruba and Igbo in the south.
Most people in the north are Muslim; most people in the south are Christian.
The north is dry grassland. The south has rainforest and the Niger Delta: the large wetland where the River Niger reaches the sea, and where most of Nigeria's oil comes from.

steps.question: Which of these is part of Nigeria's political context?

options.text: It has had military governments as well as elected ones
It has hundreds of ethnic groups

steps.right: Yes: who governs, and how, is the political context.

wrong.other: Not quite: it has had military governments as well as elected ones.
wrong.env: Not quite: that is its environmental context. Political is about government: military and elected governments.
wrong.cult: Not quite: that is its social and cultural context. Political is about government: military and elected governments.

idk.hint: Political means to do with government. Which option is about who runs the country?

steps.answerWhy: Nigeria's political context includes military governments as well as elected ones.

steps.prompt: In one line: give one reason Nigeria is important regionally and one reason it is important globally.
points: it has the biggest economy in West Africa
it exports oil around the world
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: Nigeria is regionally important with West Africa's biggest economy, and globally important as a big oil exporter.

steps.text: An economy has sectors. The primary sector takes raw materials from the land or sea: farming, fishing and oil.
The secondary sector makes things in factories: manufacturing.
The tertiary sector provides services, such as shops, banks, health care and films.

steps.question: Which sector does a taxi driver work in?
steps.right: Yes: driving people around is a service, so it is tertiary.

wrong.other: Not quite: tertiary, because a taxi provides a service.
wrong.primary: Not quite: primary takes raw materials from the land or sea. A taxi provides a service: tertiary.
wrong.secondary: Not quite: secondary makes things in factories. A taxi provides a service: tertiary.

idk.hint: Does a taxi driver take raw materials, make things, or provide a service?

steps.answerWhy: A taxi driver provides a service, so works in the tertiary sector.

steps.text: Nigeria's economy used to depend on farming. Then oil was found in the Niger Delta, and oil became the big earner.
In 2025 fuel, meaning oil and gas, made up about 86% of the goods Nigeria sold to other countries. But oil gives few jobs, because machines do most of the work.
When the world oil price falls, Nigeria's income falls with it, so depending on oil is risky.

Most of Nigeria's economy is now services. In 2025 services made up about 58% of Nigeria's economy. Industry, which in these figures includes oil as well as factories and building, made up about 16%, and farming about 23%.
Farming still gave about a third of all jobs.
Lagos is Nigeria's biggest city. Factories in and around it make food, drinks, cement and soap. Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry, based mainly in Lagos, is a growing service.

Manufacturing can stimulate development, meaning help people's lives get better. A new factory pays regular wages; workers spend them in local shops, which then need more staff; the government collects more tax for schools and roads.
One new business leading to many more jobs and more tax in this way is called the multiplier effect.

steps.question: A new cement factory opens near Lagos and pays its workers. What is the next link in the multiplier chain?

options.text: The workers spend their wages in local shops

steps.right: Yes: their spending means shops need more staff, so jobs multiply.

wrong.other: Not quite: the workers spend their wages in local shops.
wrong.close: Not quite: the chain is about growth. The workers spend their wages in local shops, which then need more staff.
wrong.abroad: Not quite: the chain stays local. The workers spend their wages in local shops, which then need more staff.

idk.hint: What do people usually do with the wages they earn?

steps.answerWhy: Workers spend their wages in local shops, which then take on more staff: the multiplier effect.

steps.prompt: In one line: how can a new factory help a country develop?
points: the wages and taxes create more jobs and services
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: Nigeria's new factories give jobs, and the wages and taxes they bring create more jobs and services: the multiplier effect.

keyPoints.heading: TNCs in Nigeria: Shell and Unilever

steps.text: A TNC, or transnational corporation, is a company that works in many countries. Its headquarters are usually in a rich country.

Shell, an oil company based in the UK, took oil from the Niger Delta on land for decades. In 2025 it sold that business to a Nigerian-owned company, but it still produces oil from deep water off the coast.
Unilever makes soap, food and drinks in factories in Nigeria, and buys from Nigerian suppliers.
TNCs give jobs and train workers in new skills. They pay taxes, and oil companies also pay the government for the oil they take. That money can fund schools and clinics.
TNCs also build roads. Bringing new technology and know-how into a country is called technology transfer.

steps.question: Which of these is an advantage of TNCs for Nigeria?

options.text: They pay taxes that can fund schools and clinics

steps.right: Yes: tax money can pay for public services.

wrong.other: Not quite: they pay taxes that can fund schools and clinics.
wrong.profit: Not quite: sending profits abroad takes money away from Nigeria. Taxes for schools and clinics are an advantage.
wrong.leak: Not quite: leaks are a disadvantage. Taxes for schools and clinics are an advantage.

idk.hint: Which option brings money that the Nigerian government can spend?

steps.answerWhy: TNCs pay taxes, which can fund schools and clinics: an advantage.

steps.text: When a foreign company sends its profits back to its home country instead of spending them where they were earned, that is profit repatriation. Less of the money then helps Nigerians.
Oil spills from pipelines, some from leaks and some from theft, have polluted creeks, farmland and fishing grounds in the Niger Delta.
Burning off the spare gas that comes up with oil, instead of using it, is called gas flaring. It wastes fuel and pollutes the air.
The picture weighs up what oil brings Nigeria and what it costs.

steps.question: An exam answer says "Shell brings jobs and money." How can it be improved?

options.text: Explain how: for example, taxes from Shell pay for schools and clinics
Add another fact: Shell is a UK company
Add an opinion: Shell is good for Nigeria

steps.right: Yes: examiners want the link to development explained, not just stated.

wrong.other: Not quite: explain how, for example taxes pay for schools and clinics.
wrong.fact: Not quite: a new fact does not explain the effect. Explain how: taxes from Shell pay for schools and clinics.
wrong.opinion: Not quite: an opinion is not an explanation. Explain how: taxes from Shell pay for schools and clinics.

idk.hint: Examiners want to know how the jobs and money help people. Which option shows a link?

steps.answerWhy: A good answer explains how: taxes from Shell pay for schools and clinics, which helps development.

steps.prompt: In one line: give one advantage and one disadvantage of TNCs for Nigeria.
points: an advantage, such as jobs or taxes
a disadvantage, such as profits leaving the country or pollution
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: TNCs in Nigeria give jobs and pay taxes, but much of the profit leaves the country and oil spills pollute the Niger Delta.

steps.text: Nigeria sells mostly oil and gas to other countries, and buys machines, vehicles and food. It used to trade mostly with Europe and the USA; now China and India are big partners too.
China has also lent money and built roads and railways in Nigeria, though some worry this leaves Nigeria in debt.

Political links have changed too. Nigeria is in the Commonwealth, a group of countries, most once ruled by Britain, that work together. It was suspended under military rule and welcomed back when elected government returned.
Nigeria is also a leading member of the African Union, which brings together the countries of Africa, and of ECOWAS.
Nigeria also receives aid: help from other countries or charities, as gifts or as loans that are cheap to pay back.
Aid given by one government directly to another is called bilateral aid, such as the UK's help for girls' schooling in Nigeria.
Aid given through international organisations, such as the World Bank (which lends for development) or the United Nations, is called multilateral aid.
Charities that run aid projects, such as handing out mosquito nets against malaria, are called NGOs: non-governmental organisations.

steps.question: The government of Japan pays for a new water supply in a Nigerian town. What type of aid is this?
steps.right: Yes: one government directly to another is bilateral.

wrong.other: Not quite: bilateral aid, from one government directly to another.
wrong.multi: Not quite: multilateral goes through an international organisation. This is one government to another: bilateral.
wrong.ngo: Not quite: NGOs are charities. This is one government to another: bilateral.

idk.hint: Bilateral means two sides: one government giving straight to another.

steps.answerWhy: One government helping another directly is bilateral aid.

steps.text: Aid can save lives and pay for schools, clinics and clean water. But it can be wasted or stolen through corruption, and may not reach the poorest people.

steps.prompt: In one line: give one good impact of aid in Nigeria and one problem with it.
points: a good impact, such as schools, clinics or mosquito nets
a problem, such as corruption or not reaching the poorest
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: aid in Nigeria pays for schools and mosquito nets, but some is lost to corruption.

keyPoints.heading: Environmental impacts and quality of life

steps.text: Development harms the environment beyond the oil spills too: factories and traffic pollute the air of Lagos, and forests are cut down for farms and buildings.
In the Ogoni area of the Niger Delta, local people protested against oil pollution. Ken Saro-Wiwa, a writer who led those peaceful protests, was executed by the military government of the time.
Development has also changed people's quality of life: how good their lives are, in health, income, schooling, housing and safety.

Life expectancy, how long a baby born now can expect to live, rose from 47 years in 2000 to 55 in 2024. Infant mortality, babies dying before their first birthday, fell from 95 to 70 in every 1,000 born alive.

steps.question: What do longer lives suggest about health care, food and clean water in Nigeria?

options.text: They have improved for many people

steps.right: Yes: people living longer is a sign of better health care, food and water.

wrong.other: Not quite: they have improved for many people.
wrong.worse: Not quite: if they had got worse, people would live shorter lives. They have improved for many.
wrong.nothing: Longer lives are a strong clue: people live longer when health care, food and water improve.

idk.hint: Do people live longer or shorter lives when health care gets better?

steps.answerWhy: Living longer suggests health care, food and clean water have improved for many people.

steps.text: But the gains are uneven. The south, with the oil and Lagos, is richer. The north is drier and mainly farming, with more poverty and fewer girls finishing school.
Boko Haram, an armed extremist group in the north-east, has attacked towns and forced many people from their homes.
The picture shows Nigeria's two halves: the drier, poorer north, and the south with the oil, the ports and the big cities.

steps.prompt: In one line: how has economic development affected Nigeria? Give one gain and one cost.
points: a gain, such as longer lives
a cost, such as pollution or uneven gains between north and south
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: development has helped Nigerians live longer, but the gains are uneven, with the north gaining less than the south.

steps.text: Now for a short quiz: six questions on the whole lesson. Take your time.

steps.question: Quiz, question 1 of 6: what kind of country is Nigeria?
steps.right: Yes: an NEE, a newly emerging economy growing as industry builds up.

wrong.w1: Not quite: Nigeria is not rich enough to be an HIC. It is an NEE.
wrong.w2: Not quite: its economy is growing as industry builds up, so it is an NEE.

steps.answerWhy: Nigeria is an NEE, a newly emerging economy.

steps.question: Quiz, question 2 of 6: where does most of Nigeria's oil come from?
steps.right: Yes: the Niger Delta, the wetland where the River Niger reaches the sea.

wrong.w1: Not quite: the north is dry grassland. The oil is in the Niger Delta.
wrong.w2: Not quite: Lagos is the biggest city. The oil is in the Niger Delta.

steps.answerWhy: Most of Nigeria's oil comes from the Niger Delta.

steps.question: Quiz, question 3 of 6: a soap factory is in which sector?
steps.right: Yes: it makes things, so secondary.

wrong.w1: Not quite: primary takes raw materials. A factory makes things: secondary.
wrong.w2: Not quite: tertiary is services. A factory makes things: secondary.

steps.answerWhy: Making things in factories is the secondary sector.

steps.question: Quiz, question 4 of 6: what is profit repatriation?

options.text: Sending profits back to the company's home country

steps.right: Yes: the profit leaves the country where it was earned.

wrong.other: Not quite: sending profits back to the company's home country.
wrong.w1: Not quite: paying tax keeps money in Nigeria. Repatriation sends profits back to the home country.
wrong.w2: Not quite: a pay rise stays in Nigeria. Repatriation sends profits back to the home country.

steps.answerWhy: Profit repatriation is a foreign company sending its profits back home.

steps.question: Quiz, question 5 of 6: aid given through the World Bank is…?
steps.right: Yes: through an international organisation, so multilateral.

wrong.w1: Not quite: bilateral is one government to another. Through the World Bank is multilateral.
wrong.w2: Not quite: NGOs are charities. Through the World Bank is multilateral.

steps.answerWhy: Aid through an international organisation is multilateral.

steps.question: Quiz, question 6 of 6: which is an environmental cost of development in Nigeria?
steps.right: Yes: air pollution, from factories and traffic.

wrong.other: Not quite: air pollution in Lagos.
wrong.w1: Not quite: jobs are a benefit. Air pollution is an environmental cost.
wrong.w2: Not quite: tax is a benefit. Air pollution is an environmental cost.

steps.answerWhy: Air pollution in Lagos, like oil spills, is an environmental cost.

steps.text: That's the end of the quiz: you got {right} out of {n}.

end.text: The lesson is finished. Tap a button to go on.
